title: Gappu's Big Ears
moral: being proud of who you are
moral_line: Be proud of who you are!
beats: Gappu the baby elephant looks at his ears and droops. Why are my ears so big?
He sees Chiku's small ears and Bandu's tiny ears and wishes his were like theirs.
The sun gets very hot. Chiku and Bandu are tired and sweaty in the jungle.
Gappu flaps his big ears - whoosh, whoosh! A cool breeze for his friends!
Chiku and Bandu cheer. Gappu stands proud. His big ears are just right.

title: Not Yet, Little Seed
beats: Aarav plants a mango seed and asks, where is my mango? The ground says: not yet!
Every morning he waters it and peeks. Still nothing. Not yet, not yet!
Aarav feels cross and wants to stop. Then he keeps watering, day after day.
Many seasons later, a big mango tree stands tall, full of yellow mangoes.
Aarav shares the sweet mangoes with everyone. Waiting was worth it!

title: The Kite in the Tree
beats: Veer and Veera fly their new kite high in the park. Up, up it goes!
Oh no - the kite gets stuck in the mango tree. Veer jumps, but it is too high.
Veera jumps too. Still too high. They both feel sad.
Gappu the elephant comes by. Veera stands on a rock, Gappu lifts his trunk, and together they free the kite.
The kite flies again, and the three of them take turns holding the string.

title: Counting Stars
beats: Night comes, and Anya does not want to go outside. The dark feels scary.
Veera holds out her hand. Come, I want to show you something.
Anya takes one small brave step, then another.
Above them, the moon glows and a hundred stars twinkle. Anya starts to count them!
Anya laughs. The night is not scary - it is full of little lights.

title: The New Girl
beats: It is Anya's first day at a new school. She stands alone, holding her bag tightly.
Everyone already has a friend. Anya looks down at her shoes and feels very small.
Meera notices Anya. She remembers how scary her own first day was.
Meera walks over, waves, and shares her storybook. Want to read with me?
Anya smiles for the first time today. By lunch, they are best friends.

title: Thank You, Mango Tree
beats: Every day, Bandu eats sweet mangoes from the big tree. Yum, yum, yum!
Chiku asks: Bandu, did you ever say thank you to the tree?
Bandu scratches his head. Thank a tree? Why?
Chiku says: it gives us shade and mangoes every day. So Bandu waters the tree.
Now every morning Bandu says thank you, tree! And the mangoes feel even sweeter.

title: Veera Says Sorry
beats: Veer is playing with his red ball in the park, bouncing it happily.
Veera wants it NOW. She snatches the ball and runs away.
Veer sits down, sad. Veera looks back and her tummy feels funny.
Veera walks back, gives the ball, and says: I am sorry, Veer.
Veer smiles. They roll the ball to each other - playing together is more fun.

title: Chiku Learns to Listen
beats: Tara has a new ball game: roll the ball, and the other one catches it at the tree.
Chiku is too excited to listen. Hop, hop, hop! She runs the wrong way.
The ball rolls past her again and again. Chiku feels cross - this game is too hard!
Tara smiles and explains once more. This time Chiku stands still and listens.
Roll... catch! Chiku gets it right. Listening made the game so much fun.

title: Veera's Promise
beats: Veera promises Chiku: after my homework, we will play ball together.
Homework done! But her friends call her to fly kites instead. Come, Veera!
Veera wants to go. Then she remembers Chiku waiting by the tree.
Veera runs to Chiku with the ball. I promised, and here I am!
Chiku hops with joy. A kept promise makes a friend feel special.

title: The Best Gift
beats: Tomorrow is Dadi's birthday. Veer wants to give her a big gift.
But his piggy bank is empty. Veer droops - what can he give?
Then he has an idea. He draws a big red heart and writes: I love you, Dadi.
He wraps it like a gift and gives it to Dadi in the morning.
Dadi hugs him and keeps it on her shelf. It is her favourite gift ever.

title: Bandu Shows Off
beats: Bandu the monkey boasts: I am the best kite flyer in the whole park!
He tugs and twirls to show off, and the kite string gets tangled. Oops!
The kite drops to the ground. Bandu feels silly and cross.
Tara quietly helps him untangle the string, knot by knot.
Bandu says thank you, Tara. This time they fly the kite together, no showing off.

title: The Thirsty Plant
beats: In Anya's classroom, a little plant sits in a pot, drooping and dry.
Nobody notices it. Anya whispers: are you thirsty, little plant?
Every morning Anya gives it a little water, and checks its leaves.
One day, the plant stands tall and green, with a new pink flower!
The whole class claps. Anya smiles - a little care made it bloom.

title: Bandu's Kind Words
beats: Bandu and Tara play catch in the jungle. Tara drops the ball. Bandu laughs: butterfingers!
Tara droops. She drops the ball again, and this time she wants to stop playing.
Bandu remembers how sad he felt when someone laughed at him.
Bandu says: sorry, Tara. You can do it - try again!
Tara tries again... and catches it! They both jump with joy. Kind words helped her.

title: Whose Turn Is It?
beats: Meera has a kite, and everyone wants a turn to fly it.
Aarav pushes in front - me first, me first!
Then he sees little Anya at the back. She has been waiting the longest.
Aarav steps back and says: Anya, you go first.
Anya's kite flies the highest of all, and everyone cheers - Aarav loudest of all.

title: Bandu and Tara's Mangoes
beats: All summer, Tara collects mangoes for the rainy days. Bandu just plays and swings.
Come play, Tara! Tara says: I will, after my work is done.
Rain comes. Bandu is hungry, but there are no mangoes left on the trees.
Tara shares her mangoes with Bandu. He says: next summer, I will help you!
Next summer, Bandu and Tara work together, then play together all evening.

title: Where Is My Book?
beats: Meera's toys and books are everywhere. Tomorrow is school, and she needs her storybook.
Morning comes. Where is my book? Not here, not there!
She is almost late. Meera looks so sad, and her room is so messy.
That evening, Meera puts every toy and book in its place.
Next morning, her book is right there on the table. Meera is the first to school!

title: Chiku and the Little Bird
beats: Chiku is eating a juicy mango when a hungry little bird lands nearby.
Chiku could eat it all, but she shares a big piece with the bird.
Later, Chiku's ball rolls into the tall grass. She looks and looks. It is lost!
The little bird flies high, spots the ball, and chirps: here, here!
Chiku gets her ball back and thanks her friend. Kindness came right back.

title: The Ball and the Pot
beats: Veer kicks his ball inside the house, even though Maa said play outside.
Bump! The ball knocks Dadi's flower pot and the little plant flops over.
Veer wants to hide the ball and say nothing. Veera looks at him and waits.
Veer takes a deep breath and tells Maa the truth: it was me, I am sorry.
Maa hugs him for being honest. Veer and Veera replant it, and soon it blooms again.

title: Aarav Claps for Meera
beats: Aarav and Meera have a running race in the park. Ready, steady, go!
Meera wins! Aarav stops and folds his arms, feeling cross.
Meera looks back at him. Her smile gets smaller.
Aarav thinks for a moment, then claps: well done, Meera!
Meera teaches him her fast-start trick, and they race again, laughing all the way.

title: Gappu's Water Shower
moral_line: Use your gifts to help others!
beats: It is so hot in the village. All the flower pots are drooping and dry.
Aarav carries water in a tiny cup, but there are too many plants.
Gappu sees him. My trunk can carry lots of water!
Gappu fills his trunk and gives every plant a gentle shower - whoosh!
The flowers stand tall again. Aarav and Gappu laugh, all wet and happy.

title: Mangoes for Everyone
beats: Chiku, Bandu and Gappu see juicy mangoes high on a tree. Yum!
Chiku jumps, but she is too small. Gappu tries, but elephants cannot climb.
Bandu climbs up, but he cannot carry the mangoes down alone.
Then they work as a team: Bandu shakes the branch, Gappu catches, Chiku collects.
A big pile of mangoes - one for each of them, and some to share!

title: Tara's New Ball
beats: Tara the bear cub gets a shiny new ball. It is mine, only mine!
Bandu and Chiku ask to play, but Tara hugs the ball and walks away.
Tara plays alone. Bounce, catch, bounce... it is boring by herself.
Tara rolls the ball to Bandu. Bandu throws to Chiku. Chiku throws back to Tara!
Now the jungle is full of laughter. The ball was more fun shared.

title: The Little Lost Kitten
moral_line: A little kindness goes a long way!
beats: One evening, Veer and Veera hear a tiny sound: meow, meow!
A little kitten sits alone, lost and shivering.
Veera gently picks it up. Veer says: let's find your home.
They walk down the lane until a happy meow answers from a doorway - its family!
The kitten purrs goodbye. Veer and Veera walk home under the stars, smiling.

title: The Thirsty Bird
beats: It is a hot summer day. A little bird sits on Aarav's window, too tired to sing.
Aarav sees its beak open. The bird is thirsty and there is no water anywhere.
Aarav puts a small bowl of water on the window, then waits quietly.
The bird drinks and drinks... then sings its happiest song.
Every morning now, the bird comes back to sing for Aarav. Kindness made a friend.
